newsitem.title: SWEDEN: H&M sees stronger European economic trends.
newsitem.headline: H&M sees stronger European economic trends.

text.p: The chief executive of Swedish fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz (H&M) said on Monday he expected European economic trends to pick up.
"I'm somewhat optimistic," chief executive Stefan Persson told Reuters. "I think I can spot some upturns, even if some markets look sluggish."

H&M plans to open about 35 stores in the autumn of 1997, including 14 in Germany, five in Austria, five in Finland, two in Norway, two in The Netherlands, one in Sweden, one in Denmark and one in Belgium.

The growth potential is significant on all markets, except in Sweden, Norway and Denmark which are more mature, Persson said. Germany, where H&M has a market share of one percent, has a large growth potential, he said.
"Sweden, Norway and Denmark are entering a more quiet phase...and Switzerland might also be a somewhat more mature market," Persson said.
In Finland, Persson expected H&M to take as large a market share as it holds in Sweden, which would mean 13-14 percent.
"We are not just stepping in there (Finland) to open five stores," he said. "I think that in the long term we have a chance to become as large as in Sweden comparatively."
Persson added that Finnish mail order sales have shown a strong development.
